newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher across the board.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher across the board.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended higher across the board on Thursday, as the yen's fall against the dollar encouraged private investors to buy, traders said.
Prices ranged from 80 to 450 yen per tonne higher at the close, with benchmark May 1998 ending 330 yen up at 13,920 yen.
The day's estimated trade volume was 54,978 lots.
September and November rose by the daily price limit of 500 yen in early afternoon trade, but retreated by the close.
Traders also said that a rally in Tokyo soybean futures accelerated buying orders in yen-based corn futures.
At 0835 GMT, the spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was $2.77-3/4 per bushel, up from the $2.76-3/4 Wednesday close.
The spot July soybean contract on the CBOT overnight trading system stood at $8.47-1/2 per bushel, against $8.47-1/4 at Wednesday's close.
